subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: Two express trains A and B start simultaneously from Stations X and Y toward Y and X respectively along parallel tracks. After crossing each other, Train A takes 4 hours 48 minutes to reach Station Y, and Train B takes 3 hours 20 minutes to reach Station X. If Train A travels at 45 km/h, what is the speed of Train B?
explanation: By the standard crossover theorem: When two bodies start simultaneously from opposite endpoints and cross each other at an intermediate point, the ratio of their speeds is given by: Speed_A / Speed_B = sqrt(Time_B_after_crossing / Time_A_after_crossing). Here Time_A = 4 hrs 48 min = 4 + 48/60 = 24/5 hours. Time_B = 3 hrs 20 min = 3 + 20/60 = 10/3 hours. Speed_A / Speed_B = sqrt( (10/3) / (24/5) ) = sqrt( (10/3) × (5/24) ) = sqrt( 50 / 72 ) = sqrt( 25 / 36 ) = 5 / 6. Given Speed_A = 45 km/h: 45 / Speed_B = 5 / 6 => Speed_B = (45 × 6) / 5 = 9 × 6 = 54 km/h.
